newsitem.title: LATVIA: Latvia in $20 mln World Bank schools loan - agency.
newsitem.headline: Latvia in $20 mln World Bank schools loan - agency.

text.p: The Baltic state of Latvia has been awarded a credit of between $20 million to $30 million for improving the standards at its schools, the Baltic News Service (BNS) said on Tuesday.

The agency quoted World Bank officials as saying the loan would be aimed at reconstructing school premises to save on energy costs, merging schools, for the assessment of teaching programmes and education reforms.
Officials from the World Bank were not available to confirm the report, which said a further credit of $18 million could be awarded in 18 months, also aimed at schools.
The agency said that Latvia will have to fund 20 percent of the projects during the first years of implementation and 30 percent later on.
It quoted a World Bank official as saying that education reforms were needed due to the increased demands of a market economy, which required more flexibility in the education system.
